notes: Claude Code ignored a top-level decision on this event from v2.1.105 until the fix in v2.1.284 (upstream: 'Claude Code ignored a top-level `decision` from `Elicitation` and `ElicitationResult` hooks from v2.1.105 until the fix in v2.1.284'). A top-level decision: 'block' also declines (upstream: 'Prints a top-level "decision": "block": the block overrides an action in the same output'). Exit 2 declines the request and no dialog appears (upstream exit-code-2 table: 'Declines the request, and no dialog appears'); 'Neither the user nor the server sees why your hook declined, because Claude Code doesn't show your stderr or your `reason`'. An accept from the hook skips the dialog (for a URL-mode request the URL never opens), and when several hooks match the same request a decline from one of them overrides an accept or cancel from another. permission_mode is NOT delivered to this event -- neither upstream example carries it, and the common-fields table makes the per-event example authoritative ('Not all events receive this field. Check the JSON example in each hook event section'). That reading is correct for permission_mode and for any UNCONDITIONAL field, but it does NOT generalise: an example depicts one call, so a CONDITIONAL field is absent from it whether or not the event delivers it, and inferring 'never delivered' from that silence is a false negative. Those live in conditional_input_fields instead -- see PreToolUse.json, where agent_id is delivered yet unshowable. Upstream documents TWO input shapes: the form-mode example recorded here, and a url-mode example identical except that it carries 'url' (e.g. https://auth.example.com/login) in place of requested_schema. The docs also list an optional elicitation_id for this event, but no Elicitation example carries it (nor, now, does the ElicitationResult example), so it is deliberately absent here rather than invented.
